_why: Dotted paths (list indexes as numbers) that may differ from a broker ledger golden, keyed <lane>/<golden> (e.g. demand/transitions); aged.json is an input, held to the merge-base's copy. Each entry names one exact path; a wildcard is refused. Empty: no difference is allowed. A PR that changes a ledger's behaviour on purpose names each path it changes here; the edit is reviewed with the PR, and the integrity job (bin/goldens/golden-integrity.py) holds the committed goldens to the merge-base tree's behaviour everywhere else, fails on an entry that explains no difference or that the merge-base already carried, and on the push to main fails until a merged change's entries are cleared. This change: records and medchron had no reply-once mark; a reply could go out twice. Both ledgers now mix in ReplyOnce and gain the nullable reply_sent_at and reply_key columns by an additive, idempotent migration, so every medchron and records schema, row and table dump gains those two columns, and reply_once.json records the mark's truth table where it said not_applicable.
